summary: This diff is purely additive Playwright E2E test infrastructure for PROJEXA's execution/field modules (dashboard, schedule, scope/BOQ, RFIs, submittals, punch-list, change-orders, site-diary, work-progress, meetings) plus supporting config (playwright.config.ts, eslint/gitignore fixes for report artifacts, package.json test:e2e script, @playwright/test devDependency) -- it touches zero product/application source code, so blast radius is genuinely low and the tier1 classification (no migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security path matches, no heavy deletion) is correct. The test code itself is unusually well-grounded: selectors and assumptions are cited to real source file:line locations, seeded-data expectations trace to the as-run Phase 1 seed scripts, and real product gaps (meetings seeded into the wrong table, work-progress never seeded, missing Label/htmlFor associations) are recorded as findings rather than papered over with weakened assertions. The RUN_MARKER/excludeSuiteWrites mechanism is a sound, deliberate answer to the real problem of write-op tests mutating a shared live org's data across repeated runs. No .github/workflows/** files are touched, and the new test:e2e script is not wired into the existing ci.yml, so this suite does not auto-execute against production in CI -- it only runs when a human/agent invokes it directly.
issues: playwright.config.ts defaults baseURL to the real live production site (https://projexa-ai.com) with no local webServer fallback unless PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL is set -- anyone running `bun run test:e2e` without that override performs real writes (new projects, RFIs, punch-list items, meetings, sprints, change orders, etc.) against production infrastructure. Scoped to a dedicated 'E2E Test Org' and consistent with the Owner-authorized Phase 1/2 testing program, but there is no cleanup/teardown of suite-created rows, so repeated runs accumulate unbounded garbage data in the live database over time.

e2e/test-data.ts commits a real, working plaintext password (MeridianE2E2026!) for two live PROJEXA accounts (OWNER/MEMBER) directly into git-tracked source. This duplicates a credential already committed in the prior merged Phase 1 PR (#45, PHASE1_SEED_REPORT.md and scripts/phase1-provision-projexa-accounts.mjs, which itself notes 'rotate after Phase 2/3 testing completes'), so it is not a new exposure introduced by this diff, but it is a second location that will need rotating together and is worth flagging since the repo, while private, has broader read access than the credential's blast radius implies.

change-orders.spec.ts's 'Send for Approval' test fills a real email field and submits a real PATCH that may trigger an actual e-signature provider request if one is configured for the org -- the test already handles both outcomes gracefully via the real HTTP response rather than assuming success, but if a paid e-signature API is wired up, repeated CI/local runs could incur real third-party costs or send real notifications.
